subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning a self-contained TypeScript module for a cyberpunk-styled riot-control armored vehicle, complete with a water cannon turret and neon light bars, using the SDK's builder, frame, rng, and glow utilities.

Now I'm working out the vehicle's dimensions and six-wheel skeleton with spin joints, plus a turret with yaw/pitch joints and hinged rear doors, alongside fictional corporate branding ("KANDRAX") and hazard-stripe decal textures for the surfaces.

I'm deciding to write my own custom paint shaders (gunmetal with yellow wear, hazard stripes) using the SDK's noise and mix tools rather than relying on prebuilt kit paints, and planning the main hull as a loft shape built from stations along the chassis bone.

Simplifying my approach, I'm opting for boxes and frustum boxes for the main body parts and sloped nose instead, and sketching out helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and glowing light strips, along with the dark gunmetal navy color for the panelled body paint.

Now I'm setting up the full color palette—armor plate gray, warning yellow, cyan and magenta accents, white, glass tint, and tire black—then laying out the chassis dimensions: lower hull box sized to clear the wheels at proper ground height, and the upper cab body positioned above it.

Working through the vehicle geometry: defining the main body box length and height, a cab section with a sloped hood frustum and raked windshield glass, plus a front ram bumper with yellow chevron paint detailing.

Working out the cab roof and windshield geometry, computing the normal direction for the tilted glass plane and sizing the rake angle at 45 degrees with the windshield length derived from the height and depth offsets.

Now I'm adding pillars, side windows with dark glass and bars for the cage, and considering whether to include doors or simple hinge joints to keep things cheap. For the hood, I'm shaping a sloped frustum box narrowing toward the front and stitching it against the lower cab body box beneath the windshield to form the combined front structure.

Shaping the windshield and hood slope with a frustum box, then setting wheel positions along the front-to-rear body length.

Working out wheel placement so wheels slightly overlap the body sides with matching fender arches, and designing the armored wheel assembly with a tire cylinder, rim, neon cyan ring, and bolt details mounted via rotated joints along the x-axis.

Now I'm adding underglow rods, skirt armor plates between the wheels, and a decal plane for a corporate logo on the body sides, working through how the plane's normal direction needs to face outward on each side so the text reads correctly from either viewpoint.

Confirming text runs toward the front on the -X side too, reading correctly in both orientations. Now I'm designing the roof details: a full-width light bar at the cab roof front with alternating magenta/cyan strobe segments and glow, plus a water cannon turret mounted on the forward part of the cargo roof with a base ring, yaw/pitch joints, and a long barrel extending over the cab at a height that clears the roofline.

Still adding roof details — tapered barrel with glowing cyan rings, a lathed nozzle, hose coupling, two horizontal water tank cylinders on the rear roof with decal labels like "H2O 12,000L," roof rails, antenna array, camera domes, sirens, a rear light bar/spoiler, double doors with hinge joints and handles, a rear ram bar, magenta tail light strips, and a front push bar with yellow chevron paint stripes.

I'm designing slit cyan headlight glow bars with magenta DRLs, a dark mesh grille with a logo decal, a fictional license plate texture ("KX-2077 / CORP SEC"), side mirrors, door handles, ladder rungs, fender-mounted smoke launcher cylinders, A-pillar spotlights, barred windows, and a roof ID sticker. I'm also laying out the rig's joint hierarchy — chassis, six wheels, front doors, rear doors, yaw/pitch, nozzle, and hatch — and assigning roles to each joint.

Keeping wheel joints as hinge-type, I'm targeting roughly 200 parts total using helper loops, and planning out six to eight glowing textures including a corporate hexagon logo emblem, windshield HUD, side decal text ("RIOT CONTROL / KANDRAX SECURITY"), license plate, gauge cluster, a rear LED board flashing "DISPERSE," a grille emblem, and a roof billboard reading "DISPERSE • COMPLY." Now I'm writing the hull paint function with gunmetal base coloring, procedural noise mottling, and computed panel seam grids.

Writing paint shaders...

Adding more helper functions...

Now I'm sketching out the hull geometry piece by piece: a skid plate under the chassis, then the lower hull box, building up the vehicle's body structure layer by layer.

Continuing to lay out boxes for the cargo section and cab, figuring out how the roof, pillars, and side panels fit together so the window openings aren't blocked.

Still placing door panels...

Now I'm figuring out the windshield geometry, sizing a slanted box and working out its rotation and position so the top and bottom edges land at the right slope coordinates.

Then I'm adding details like wiper rods and frame trim, plus a semi-transparent HUD plane offset slightly off the windshield surface with cyan markings and a brand mark, giving it a soft glow while keeping the transparent areas see-through. Moving on to the hood as a frustum shape, a dark front fascia box, a grille with neon cyan slats, and a hazard-striped front bumper ram positioned near the vehicle's nose.

I'm positioning a push-bar with two upright rods and a yellow cross bar over the fascia, along with cyan slit headlights and magenta DRL strips plus corner lights. For the wheel arches, I'm working out the geometry so the arch covers sit correctly above each tire based on wheel position, tire width, and hub radius, making sure they align with the body's lower hull dimensions.

For armor skirts between the wheels, I'm calculating gap positions between front and rear wheel spans and finding the gaps too small to warrant skirt plates, so I'll skip that detail.

For the cargo box, I'm placing side text and neon panels on the upper sides, computing dimensions based on cargo box width to position them correctly.

Now I'm designing the rear doors: hinge joints at the back corners, door panels with painted hull color, window slits with bars, and handles. I'm deciding to put the LED billboard on the roof rear edge instead of the swinging doors to avoid clashing with door motion, plus adding a rear bumper with hazard stripes and magenta tail light strips at the corners.

Moving to the roof, I'm laying out the cargo roof panel, roof rails, and a light bar on the cab roof with alternating cyan and magenta glowing segments facing both front and rear. Then I'm building the turret: a base ring with yaw and pitch joints positioned correctly along the Y and X axes, cradle plates, and a barrel swept along the z-axis.

Still writing turret details... I'm defining the breech box, tapered barrel rod, and a lathed nozzle profile with glowing cyan rings spaced along the barrel, plus a sweep for the water hose and two horizontal cylindrical tanks mounted behind the turret with bands and capped ends.

Now I'm working out tank materials and cyberpunk styling (dark teal body with glowing cyan stripe rings), feed pipes from tanks to turret, a small gauge panel on the tank's front cap, plus roof extras like an antenna, camera dome, A-pillar spotlights, and a rear LED billboard sign mounted on posts positioned to avoid clipping the tanks.

Now I'm adding smoke/gas launcher tube banks tilted forward on the cab roof, side mirror arms with mirror boxes, a glowing cyan rim ring on the wheels, and starting the wheel joint generation loop that builds front and rear wheel names and positions.

Still writing wheel geometry...

With other parts factored in, we'd hit roughly 400 total, well under the 1000 limit, so I'll trim tread count to 12 and lugs to 5 to stay safe. I'm also sketching a hexagonal logo emblem outlined in yellow with a "K" shape for the corporate "KANDRAX" brand.

I'm also laying out the side panel text, HUD overlay with brackets and targeting readouts, an LED display with warning messages like "DISPERSE" and "COMPLY," a license plate design, and a circular gauge dial.

Writing plane placement helper...

For the front fascia I'm planning a dark box with thin cyan neon slats and a logo decal plus a lidar puck on the bull bar, then sketching a hazard stripe paint pattern using a procedural diagonal function.

Now I'm adding grime via a noise-based mix to weather the hazard stripe texture, then starting the hull paint shader with a base noise-blended color and panel seam lines computed from surface normals.

Still writing hull paint shader...

Adding a yellow warning stripe along the lower hull where it's horizontal, and planning to reuse similar materials with slight color variations for armor panels versus the darker steel base.

Defining more paint colors...

For geometry, I'm adding dome-shaped camera sensors on the roof using half-sphere geometry, and making sure the wheel bottoms touch y=0 so the model sits properly on the ground.

Checking overall height: roof around 2.14, sign up to 2.7, turret near 2.9, antenna to 3.3 total. I'm also setting up a water nozzle glow effect and a hose path sweeping from the tank to the turret base, plus defining hinge joints and panel placement for the rear doors.

Now I'm placing door window slits, handles, logos, and hazard strips, then catching a z-depth overlap between the rear bumper and door panel -- I'm shifting the bumper's z position and depth and raising the door panel's vertical range to resolve the collision.

Checking tail light placement against the body's outer edge near the door hinge, then verifying the front fender and wheel clearance under the hood frustum -- the wheel pokes out slightly from the hood's half-width, which seems acceptable.

Now I'm positioning the bull bar's yellow tube frame with uprights, a top cross rod, and diagonal braces, then placing the plow bumper box to confirm it fits within the fascia boundary, locking the overall vehicle length at -3.13 on the z-axis.

Checking that the total length rounds to about 6.2 meters, which feels appropriately long for an "interceptor" build. I'm placing license plates at the front and rear bumper planes, then working out the fuel gauge position relative to the tank's front end, making sure it clears the turret base and barrel breech, before sizing a cylindrical tank detail along the Z axis.

Still writing tank details...

I'll skip the glass tube gauge and hose coupler details, then add a small sensor dome with a magenta glow lens on the cab roof near the turret barrel. Now I'm writing out the full code, aiming to keep it around 400-500 lines with metadata export included.

I'll decide against using rng for scatter decals or warning stickers to avoid unused imports, and instead write a helper function for creating rod-shaped bones with configurable color and segment count, typing color parameters loosely to avoid strict Fill type issues.

Now I'm building the door structure: a hinge joint at the front corners, with a lower panel box, trim rails, and glass positioned along the door frame, adjusting heights for the top rail and window placement.

Still writing door geometry...

Now I'm setting neon glow intensity to 1.2 and laying out the headlight assembly: a cyan glow box, a magenta DRL strip, and a dark housing positioned slightly behind them in z so the housing reads as the base and the glows sit in front.

Working through overlaps with the bumper and fascia, I'm adjusting the DRL and cyan glow y-positions so they clear the bumper top and sit within the hood frustum's front face height, then setting the housing center and height to match.

Now I'm reworking the grille since the taller bumper would cover it — shrinking the bumper height and repositioning the grille box above it, then figuring out how to place the logo plane and slats so they don't overlap, settling on horizontal rod slats spaced across the center while leaving room for the logo.

I'm deciding to skip putting the logo on the sloped hood top since the geometry gets messy, and instead plan to place it on the doors and rear, plus adding a license plate plane positioned low on the front bumper.

I'm checking which API functions actually exist before using them, settling on lathe for rounded parts and glow for emphasis, and deciding to skip extra pose rotations except maybe a slightly ajar rear door. I'll also add roof rack bars and side-step bars, then write the final code.
